newsitem.title: UK: Brazil coffee crop estimate fails to stir traders.
newsitem.headline: Brazil coffee crop estimate fails to stir traders.

text.p: Coffee traders were not surprised by a report quoting official sources as saying Brazil's 1997/98 coffee crop would total only 20 million bags.
The estimate compares with 22 million bags forecast by the Brazilian government earlier.

"While the Brazilian crop estimate reported yesterday was pegged at 20 million bags, it has to be remembered that lower estimates are not unusual from local producers for obvious reasons," said broker GNI in a commentary on Thursday.

The report on the estimated crop was referred to by German statistician F.O. Licht in its latest daily review which also cited the comment that the reduction was due to the bi-annual nature of coffee production.
Other traders said a crop figure of between 20 and 25 million had been talked about. "I don't think this came as a surprise," said one.
Another said it was not clear how official was the source quoted by the report.
Forecasts of the 1997/98 crop have ranged from just below 20 million to as much as 28 million, with the U.S. Department of Agriculture for example looking at the top of that range.
